members_note: Sahel, Guinea coast and Central Africa; SOM an odd member
el_nino_signal: drier in the Sahel (-0.42 mm/day/degC; -0.73 for Eastern Pacific El Nino, -0.12 for Central Pacific); Guinea coast drier
mechanism: Tropospheric-temperature mechanism; a high-pressure anomaly over the tropical Atlantic whose easterlies cut moisture transport into the Sahel; El Nino with an Atlantic Nina gives a Guinea-coast-dry / Sahel-wet dipole whose Sahel side is offset by the tropospheric warming. The link is not stationary (r -0.43 in 1931-70 vs -0.59 in 1971-2010), modulated by the AMV, the IPO and Mediterranean SST. SOM is an odd member: its Oct-Dec rains behave like East (wetter).
references: Cai et al. 2025; Rowell 2001; Janicot, Trzaska & Poccard 2001; Giannini, Saravanan & Chang 2003; Joly & Voldoire 2009; Rodriguez-Fonseca et al. 2015

season: May-Oct (Guinea-coast bimodal rains; monsoon in northern Nigeria)
stage: developing; the state of ENSO in boreal spring matters (decay of the previous event or onset of the next)
main_lag: concurrent to a few months (L ~ 0 to +3)
el_nino_signal: drier (Guinea coast); La Nina wetter in Jun-Sep
mechanism: As West: Atlantic Nina co-occurrence (Guinea-coast drying), tropospheric warming, subsidence. Remnant SST anomalies of a decaying event can carry into the following summer (the 1983 Sahel drought after the 1982/83 El Nino). Eastern Pacific El Nino also dries the Guinea coast in Dec-Feb.
references: Cai et al. 2025; Rodriguez-Fonseca et al. 2011, 2015; Joly & Voldoire 2009; Chang et al. 2006

members_note: ETH SDN SSD: Ethiopian plateau and Sudan; COG GIN GNB SLE: Guinea coast and Congo
mechanism: Ethiopia and Sudan: the tropospheric-temperature mechanism (a more stable atmosphere suppresses convection); Rossby waves weaken the Tropical Easterly Jet, so less upper-level divergence over the Horn; the Somali Jet starts later and is weaker. Guinea-coast members: El Nino often comes with an Atlantic Nina, so a drier Guinea coast, plus subsidence from upper-level convergence over West Africa.
references: Cai et al. 2025; Gleixner et al. 2017; Diro, Grimes & Black 2011; Rodriguez-Fonseca et al. 2015

season: Oct-Dec short rains; Mar-May long rains
stage: short rains: developing to mature (about 2 months before the peak); long rains: decay (+3 to +5 months)
main_lag: concurrent (L ~ 0, from -2 to +2) in Oct-Dec; weak and inconsistent in Mar-May
el_nino_signal: wetter in Oct-Dec (+0.38 mm/day/degC), still wetter in Dec-Feb (+0.29); long rains: little signal after El Nino, drier during multi-year Central Pacific La Nina
mechanism: Weaker Walker circulation induces a positive Indian Ocean Dipole: easterlies along the equatorial Indian Ocean, a warm western Indian Ocean and a stronger ITCZ there bring more moist convergence onto the East African coast. In Dec-Feb the South Indian Convergence Zone and its cloud bands move north-east, off southern Africa. ENSO-IOD coupling sets the strength of the link (r 0.30 in 1931-70 vs 0.61 in 1971-2010).
references: Cai et al. 2025; Saji et al. 1999; Black, Slingo & Sperber 2003; Goddard & Graham 1999; Palmer et al. 2023

members: AGO COD MOZ MWI NAM ZMB ZWE
members_note: CIV (Guinea coast) and the COD interior are odd members
stage: mature and decay (from the peak to about 3 months after)
el_nino_signal: drier: Oct-Dec -0.15, Dec-Feb -0.37, Mar-May -0.19 mm/day/degC; Eastern Pacific El Nino much stronger than Central Pacific (Dec-Feb -0.70 vs -0.003 mm/day)
mechanism: Warming over the Indian Ocean basin weakens the ocean-land pressure gradient, so seasonal convergence weakens. The South Indian Convergence Zone shifts north-east; fewer tropical-temperate troughs; the Angola Low weaker and shifted north; the Botswana High stronger; the Mozambique Channel Trough shallower; negative SAM in Dec-Feb. Opposite pole to East in Oct-Dec and Dec-Feb. The link is not stationary (r 0.15 in 1931-70 vs -0.69 in 1971-2010) and varies from event to event (1997/98). CIV (Guinea coast) and the COD interior are odd members.
references: Cai et al. 2025; Cook 2000; Cretat et al. 2019; Driver & Reason 2017; Blamey et al. 2018; Hart, Washington & Reason 2018
